title: Global and local complete intersections over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field. For a commutative ring $T$ and $g\in T$ let $T_g=T[1/g]$ be the localization of $T$ at the element $g$, i.e. at the multiplicative subset $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], a $k$-algebra when $T$ is; let $\dim T$ be the Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (so $\dim T=-\infty$ iff $T=0$), and $D(g)=\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}T:g\notin\mathfrak q\}$. (1) A commutative $k$-algebra $T$ is a *global complete intersection over $k$* if $T=0$, or if there are integers $n,c\ge0$, polynomials $f_1,\dots,f_c\in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and an isomorphism of $k$-algebras $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\cong T$ such that $\dim T=n-c$. (Such a $T$ is in particular a finitely generated $k$-algebra; the convention that the zero ring is a global complete intersection is part of the definition, Stacks 00S9.) (2) Let $S$ be a finitely generated $k$-algebra. $S$ is a *local complete intersection over $k$* if there is a family $(g_i)_{i\in J}$ of elements of $S$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}S=\bigcup_{i\in J}D(g_i)$ and each $S_{g_i}$ is a global complete intersection over $k$ in the sense of (1).

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks Algebra Definition 00S9 (algebra.tex 35817-35831; tag verified in tags/tags) and the remark after it (35833-35849). Content agrees: presentation k[x_1..x_n]/(f_1..f_c) with dim = n - c, zero ring a global complete intersection by convention, local complete intersection via a covering Spec S = U D(g_i) with each S_{g_i} global c.i. Two changes: (a) stmt_deps: S_g is the localization of a ring at an element, so def-weil-pbc-module-localization (localization of modules at a multiplicative subset) is replaced by the ring node def-weil-ring-localization-away (Mathlib leaf Localization.Away); (b) clause (1) is now stated for any commutative k-algebra T rather than for a finitely generated one, so that applying it to S_{g_i} in clause (2) needs no hidden claim that S_{g_i} is finitely generated (a presentation makes T finitely generated anyway; Stacks applies (1) to S_{g_i} tacitly); the meaning of dim for T = 0 (-infinity) is made explicit. No claim inside the definition: the definition is two existence conditions and a convention, so nothing moved to statement nodes and no pointers. Not added (not part of the definition): the remark after 00S9 that a global c.i. of dimension n - c has dim S_m = n - c at every maximal ideal and is equidimensional, and Lemma 00SA (localization preserves global/local c.i.). Citers: lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-over-field-dimension-at-points (step 2) uses only the bare definition (2); lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-local-complete-intersection states the bare definition; lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-free-rank-codimension (Stacks 00SC (1)=>(4)) will need, when split, the equidimensionality remark after 00S9 (t = m - dim S_g = height(q'') - height(q) uses dim (S_g)_q-local = dim S_g) and Lemma 00SA-type facts: these are for its split, not this node.
